text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS @

- Hungarian Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs and his visiting Romanian counterpart Adrian Severin agreed in Budapest on Friday to reopen the Hungarian consulate general in Cluj and the Romanian consulate in Debrecen that had been closed some years ago. The ministers exchanged the ratification documents of the basic treaty between the two countries.
- Smallholder MP Miklos K. Csontos was stabbed to death in his home by his son-in-law on Friday evening.
- Executives of the Hungarian State Railways and the Railworkers' Union Sunday agreed on a 18 percent wage increase for 1997. @
- A temperature of -29 Celsius was recorded in Putnok, northeast of Hungary, on Sunday, matching a 100-year low.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn Saturday nominated journalist Tibor Thurzo for the post of vice-president of Hungarian TV.
- Smallholder President Jozsef Torgyan Friday described the current year as one marked by chaos, bringing the Hungarian economy to the brink of collapse. (Sat.)
NEPSZABADSAG @

- The Young Democrats are now on top along with the Socialist Party with the support of 16 percent of those surveyed in a recent Sonda Ipsos poll. The Smallholders' popularity has declined after a four-month rise to 13 percent. The Free Democrats had 8, the Christian Democrats 4 and the Democratic Forum 2 percent of support.
- Civil servants will receive a 17 percent salary hike, with the extent of the various supplements ranging from 10-50 percent. @
- Fuel sales dropped by 11 percent in the first ten months of 1996 compared to January-October last year, said Laszlo Molnar, director of the Energy Information Office. (Sat.)

- A consortium comprising German, Hungarian and Swedish businessmen tried to illegally transfer $30 million to their subsidiaries' accounts at a Hungarian bank in Budapest on December 21, using a bogus certificate of cover from a French bank. The swindlers were caught.
MAGYAR NEMZET @
- The Independent Police Trade Union Friday said they may stage a public protest unless the police are granted about HUF 4 billion necessary for wage increases next year.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- More Hungarian companies plan to increase their production capacity in the next six months than a year ago, according to a report by the National Labour Centre.
- Hungarian companies have to pay the highest wage-related costs in Europe, according to a survey by management consultants Czipin & Partner. @
- The Hungarian oil and gas company MOL will explore and produce oil and gas from a 5,000 sq km field in Syria next year.
- The trading volume on the Budapest Commodity Exchange reached a record high value of HUF 25 billion on Friday.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Polgari Bank, a subsidiary of Budapest Bank, has been bought back from GE Capital by the Finance Ministry. Ministry State Secretary Tibor Draskovits neither confirmed nor denied the news. @
- A Hungarian bank consortium will extend a $160 million loan with a term of six months to the Russian giant Gazprom.
- Eight subsidiaries of the agricultural giant Babolna Rt will merge with the parent company as of January 1.
